newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Apartheid police chief to be called to truth body.
newsitem.headline: Apartheid police chief to be called to truth body.

text.p: Ex-police chief Adriaan Vlok will become the first cabinet minister from the old South African apartheid regime to be forced to testify to the truth commission, officials said on Thursday.

Archbishop Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, trying to clear up and heal the country's murky past, will on Friday subpoena Vlok and eight former senior police to appear at closed hearings of the body.
Tutu's deputy, Alex Boraine, told a news conference that Vlok and the others would be asked to tell all they know about human rights violations under apartheid.
He said the decision was taken after the police generals failed to submit satisfactory written evidence on the actions of police under white rule.
"The subpoenas are ready. The process will start on Friday -- it will be a matter of finding the people," said Boraine.
Vlok's name was added to the list because allegations were made against him at a number of the commission's public hearings for victims of human rights abuses.
"We will be asking him a number of questions about the allegations that have been made," Boraine said.
Vlok was in charge of the police at the height of emergency rule in the mid 1980s when up to 30,000 people were detained at any one time amid countless allegations of torture in prisons.
Many of the alleged victims have been telling their stories to the truth commission, which has so far heard far less than it hoped from those who carried out the abuses.
The commission has the power to compensate victims and grant amnesty to perpetrators who confess.

Boraine said former police commissioners Johan van der Merwe, Mike Geldenhuys, Johan Coetzee and Hennie de Witt as well as senior generals Basie Smit, Johan le Roux, Krappies Engelbrecht and Bertus Steyn would be summoned.
It will be up to the commission to decide whether to go public with their testimony after the closed hearings. More former policemen will be subpoenaed later.
